summary: Find files by name pattern under a path, optionally filtered by recent modification.

modifiedWithin.description: Only files modified within this window, e.g. 7d.

posix.semanticNotes: Emitted as `find <path> -name <name>`. `modifiedWithin` is NOT rendered to argv here: find expects `-mtime -7` (days) and the value (e.g. "7d") needs unit parsing the structured arg form can't express. The @node search adapter, or a call-site translation to -mtime, handles modifiedWithin; left out of posix argv on purpose rather than emitting a wrong flag.

powershell.semanticNotes: DIVERGES: -Filter uses Windows wildcard semantics (different from POSIX glob edge cases) and modifiedWithin requires a downstream Where-Object on LastWriteTime, which the structured arg form can't express. Recursive by default here to match `find`'s descent.

node.semanticNotes: The @node search adapter is the only place modifiedWithin (e.g. 7d/24h) is parsed and applied uniformly across platforms.

summary: Search file contents for a text pattern, recursively by default.

path.description: File or directory to search in.

posix.semanticNotes: `-e <text>` passes the pattern safely even when it starts with a dash. grep uses POSIX basic regex by default; treat `text` as a regex, not a literal.

powershell.semanticNotes: DIVERGES: Select-String uses .NET regex (not POSIX BRE) and is recursive only when -Path is a wildcard or with Get-ChildItem piping; the `recursive` flag has no direct -Recurse equivalent here. Regex dialect and recursion both differ from grep.
